units.summary: Converts a string to camel case. Camel case is the naming convention in which the first word is written in lowercase and each subsequent word begins with a capital letter, concatenated without any separator characters.

params.name: str
params.doc: The string that is to be changed to camel case.

guarantees.text: "welcome to our website" gives "Welcome to our website"

units.summary: Converts a string by replacing special characters and diacritical marks with their ASCII equivalents. For example, "Crème brûlée" becomes "Creme brulee". Only Latin letters are converted. Letters of other scripts, such as Hangul, Cyrillic, or Greek, are kept as they are, even if they carry diacritical marks.

params.name: str
params.doc: The input string to be deburred.

guarantees.text: "München" gives "Munchen", "Crème brûlée" gives "Creme brulee" and "mañana" gives "manana"

units.summary: Converts the characters "&", "<", ">", '"', and "'" in `str` to their corresponding HTML entities. For example, "<" becomes "<".

guarantees.text: ""Hello"" (the word Hello in double quotes) gives ""Hello""
the word Hello in single quotes gives the word Hello surrounded by "'" on both sides

units.summary: Escapes the RegExp special characters "^", "$", "\", ".", "*", "+", "?", "(", ")", "[", "]", "{", "}", and "|" in `str`.

guarantees.text: "Hello." gives "Hello" followed by one backslash and a dot
"(test)" gives "test" wrapped in an escaped opening parenthesis and an escaped closing parenthesis, each preceded by one backslash
"[abc]" gives "abc" wrapped in an escaped opening bracket and an escaped closing bracket, each preceded by one backslash
"user@domain.com" gives "user@domain" followed by one backslash and ".com"

units.summary: Converts a string to lower case. Lower case is the naming convention in which each word is written in lowercase and separated by an space ( ) character.

params.name: str
params.doc: The string that is to be changed to lower case.

guarantees.text: "Hello World" gives "hello world" and "camelCase" gives "camel case"
"some-kebab-case" gives "some kebab case", "PascalCase" gives "pascal case" and "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" gives "screaming snake case"
"user_profile-settings" gives "user profile settings" and " mixed CASE text " gives "mixed case text"

units.summary: Pads string on the left and right sides if it's shorter than length. Padding characters are truncated if they can't be evenly divided by length. If the length is less than or equal to the original string's length, or if the padding character is an empty string, the original string is returned unchanged.

params.name: length
params.doc: The length of the resulting string once padded.

params.name: chars
params.doc: The character(s) to use for padding.

guarantees.text: "abc" padded to `length` 8 without `chars` gives "abc" with two spaces on the left and three spaces on the right
"abc" padded to `length` 9 with `chars` "123" gives "123abc123" and to `length` 10 gives "123abc1231"

units.summary: Converts a string to Pascal case. Pascal case is the naming convention in which each word is capitalized and concatenated without any separator characters.

params.name: str
params.doc: The string that is to be changed to pascal case.

units.summary: Reverses a given string. This function takes a string as input and returns a new string that is the reverse of the input.

params.name: value
params.doc: The string that is to be reversed.

guarantees.text: "hello" gives "olleh", "world" gives "dlrow" and "hello world" gives "dlrow olleh"

units.summary: Converts the first character of each word in a string to uppercase and the remaining characters to lowercase. Start case is the naming convention in which each word is written with an initial capital letter.

guarantees.text: "hello world" gives "Hello World" and "HELLO WORLD" gives "Hello World"
"XMLHttpRequest" gives "Xml Http Request", "_abc_123_def" gives "Abc 123 Def" and "12abc 12ABC" gives "12 Abc 12 Abc"

units.summary: Removes leading and trailing whitespace or specified characters from a string.

params.name: str
params.doc: The string from which characters will be trimmed.

params.name: chars
params.doc: The character(s) to remove from the string. Can be a single character or an array of characters.

guarantees.text: " hello " gives "hello" and a tab, newline and spaces around "hello" are removed too
throws an error when `chars` is a string whose length is not 1

units.summary: Converts the HTML entities `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, and `'` in `str` to their corresponding characters. It is the inverse of `escape`.

guarantees.text: "This is a <div> element." gives "This is a <div> element."
"This is a "quote"" gives "This is a "quote"" (with plain double quotes)
"'" is converted to a plain single quote
"This is a & symbol" gives "This is a & symbol"
""Hello & Welcome" <says the > user" gives ""Hello & Welcome" <says the > user"

units.summary: Converts a string to upper case. Upper case is the naming convention in which each word is written in uppercase and separated by an space ( ) character.

params.name: str
params.doc: The string that is to be changed to upper case.

guarantees.text: "camelCase" gives "CAMEL CASE" and "some whitespace" gives "SOME WHITESPACE"

units.summary: Splits `string` into an array of its words, treating spaces and punctuation marks as separators.
